name: Sikagard-550 W Elastic
paste:
SIKAGARD®-550 W ELASTIC: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikagard®-550 W Elastic, April 2023, Version 02.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/m/sikagard_-550_w_elastic.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikagard®-550 W Elastic where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.02).
1.2 Product description.
    - Sikagard®-550 W Elastic is a one component, plasto-elastic coating based on UV-curing acrylic dispersion with excellent crack-bridging properties even at temperatures below 0 °C.
    - Sikagard®-550 W Elastic complies with the requirements of EN 1504-2 as protective coating.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikagard®-550 W Elastic is used for protection and enhancement of concrete structures (normal and lightweight concrete), especially exposed outdoor concrete surfaces with a risk of cracking. Sikagard®-550 W Elastic is used with concrete repair works as an elastic protective coating on Sika® smoothing mortar (refer to relevant product / system data sheet), fibre cement and overcoating of existing soundly adhering coatings
    - Suitable for protection against ingress (Principle 1, method 1.3 of EN 1504-9),
    - Suitable for moisture control (Principle 2, method 2.3 of EN 1504-9)
    - Suitable for increasing the resistivity (Principle 8, method 8.3 of EN 1504-9)
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikagard®-550 W Elastic
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: CRACK BRIDGING, ANTI-CARBONATION PROTECTIVE COATING FOR CONCRETE
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - EN 1504-2 performance testing, LPM Report A-33’882- 2 dated July 09
    - The product is included in a compilation of tested products and systems as per
    - OS 5a (OS DII) at the German Institute of Road Systems
    - Determination of dynamic crack bridging properties according to EN 1062-7, report P8690a dated 27/08/2014, Kiwa Polymer Institut GmbH
    - Protective coating according to EN 1504-2, DoP 02 03 03 03 002 0 000003 1125; certified by Factory Production Control Body: 0921; certificate 0921-BPR-2046 and provided with the CE-mark
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 1504-2: cited elsewhere in the data sheet; listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1); Description (p.1).
    - EN 1504-9: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Uses (p.1).
    - EN 1062-7: listed under approvals, certificates or standards; test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1); Technical Information > Crack bridging ability (p.2).
    - AS/NZS 4548.5: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Crack bridging ability (p.2); Technical Information > Permeability to carbon dioxide (p.2); Technical Information > Permeability to water vapour (p.2).
    - EN 1542: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 1062-3: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Capillary absorption (p.2).
    - EN 1062-11: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Behaviour after artificial weathering (p.2).
    - EN 13687: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Freeze thaw de-icing salt resistance (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Crack-bridging even at low temperatures (-20°C)
    - High diffusion resistance against CO2 reducing the rate of carbonation
    - Water vapour permeable
    - Very good resistance against weathering and ageing
    - Environmentally friendly (solvent free)
    - Reduced tendency to dirt pick up and contamination
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Acrylate dispersion
    - Appearance and colour: Thixotropic liquid available in almost every colour shade.
    - Density: ~ 1.30 kg/l (at +20°C)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Solid content by mass: ~ 65%
    - Solid content by volume: ~ 53%
    - Tensile strain at break: Elongation at break; at room temperature (not exposed to weathering): 120%; at -20°C: 70%
    - Tensile adhesion strength: 2.9 (2.8) N/mm² (EN 1542)
    - Capillary absorption: w = 0.02 kg/(m²h0.5) (EN 1062-3)
    - Behaviour after artificial weathering: Pass after 2000 hours (EN 1062-11)
    - Freeze thaw de-icing salt resistance: 2.9 (2.1) N/mm² (EN 13687 part 1 & part 2)
2.7 Crack bridging ability. Class A1 (-20°C) - 2 coats; Class B2 (-15°C) - 3 coats

    | Crack Width at Break | 1.5 mm |
    | Crack Bridging Ability | 5.0 |
    Test method printed: (EN 1062-7)
    Test method printed: (AS/NZS 4548.5)
    Test method printed: Appendix F

2.10 System structure.
    | System | Product ¹⁾ | Number of applications |
    | Priming ²⁾ | Sikagard®-552 W | 1 |
    | Aquaprimer |
    | Top coat ³⁾ | Sikagard®-550 W Elastic | 2 – 3 |
    | 1) Please refer to the respective product data sheet for additional information. |
    | A third coat is also required in order to achieve the required thickness for full durability (crack bridging, adhesion after thermal cycling, etc.) |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
    2) For very difficult substrate (very dense or weak with tensile strength < 1 N/mm2) and at low temperature, use solvent containing primer Sikagard®- 551 S Elastic Primer.
    3) In case of an intensive yellow or red colour shade and/or a dark substrate, more than two coats might be required.
2.11 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 15 lt plastic pail
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production if stored properly in undamaged and unopened original sealed packaging.
    - Storage conditions: Store in cool and dry conditions. Protect from direct sunlight and frost.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Exposed concrete without existing coating.
    - The surface must be dry, sound and free from loose and friable particles.
    - Suitable preparation methods are steam cleaning, high pressure water jetting or blastcleaning.
    - New concrete must be at least 28 days old.
    - If required, a levelling pore sealer (e.g. Sika® MonoTop®-723 N, Sika® Monotop FC, Sikagard®-720 EpoCem® etc.) shall be applied – refer to the respective product data sheet. For cement based products, allow a curing time of at least 4 days before coating (except when the EpoCem is used, then coating can be applied within 24 hours).
3.3 Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Exposed concrete with existing coating.
    - Existing coatings must be tested to confirm their adhesion to the substrate and their suitability - adhesion test average > 0.8 N/mm2 with no single value below 0.5 N/mm2.
    - For water based coating, use Sikagard-552 W AquaPrimer as primer.
    - For solvent based coating, use Sikagard-551 S Elastic Primer as primer.
    - In case of doubt, carry out adherence testing to determine which primer is most suitable – wait at least 2 weeks prior to conduct the adhesion test - an average value of 0.8 N/mm² is required with no single value below 0.5 N/mm².

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Applied product ready for use: Full cure: ~ 7 days at +20°C
4.3 Consumption.
    | Product | Per coat |
    | Sikagard®-552 W Aquaprimer | ~ 0.10 - 0.15 kg/m² |
    | Sikagard®-550 W Elastic | ~ 0.25 - 0.35 kg/m² |
4.4 Layer thickness. Minimum required dry film thickness to achieve the required characteristics (CO2 equivalent air thickness of 50 m) ≈ 160 μm. Minimum required dry film thickness to achieve full durability characteristics (CO2 diffusion, adhesion after thermal cycling and crack bridging) ≈ 340 μm.
4.5 Waiting time to overcoating. Waiting time between coats at +20°C substrate temperature:
    | Previous coating | Waiting time | Next coating |
    | Sikagard®-552 W | 5 hours min. | Sikagard®-550 W Elastic |
    | Aquaprimer |
    | Sikagard®-550 W Elastic | 8 hours min. | Sikagard®-550 W Elastic |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Note: When application is on existing coatings, the waiting time for both primers will increase by 100%.
    Refresher coats of Sikagard®-550 W Elastic can be applied without priming if the existing coat has been thoroughly cleaned.
4.6 Application.
    - Apply Sikagard®-552 W AquaPrimer evenly onto the substrate.
    - Sikagard®-550 W Elastic can be applied by brush, roller or airless spray.
    - For more details, refer to Protective Coating Application Method Statement.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment.
    - Clean all tools and application equipment with clean water immediately after use.
    - Hardened / cured material can only be removed mechanically.
    - For Sikagard®-551 S Elastic Primer use Sika® Thinner C.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations - Do not apply when there is.
    - Expected rain
    - Relative humidity > 80%
    - Temperature below +8°C and/or below dew point
    - Concrete younger than 28 days
    The system is resistant to aggressive atmospheric influences.
    Dark colour shades (especially black, dark red and blue, etc.) may fade more rapidly than other lighter tone colours. Refreshing coat might be required at earlier interval than usual.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +8°C min. / +35°C max.
5.3 Relative air humidity. < 80%
5.4 Dew point. Temperature must be at least 3°C above dew point.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +8°C min. / +35°C max.
5.6 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - Expected rain
    - Relative humidity > 80%
    - Temperature below +8°C and/or below dew point
5.7 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - Existing coatings must be tested to confirm their adhesion to the substrate and their suitability - adhesion test average > 0.8 N/mm2 with no single value below 0.5 N/mm2.
    - In case of doubt, carry out adherence testing to determine which primer is most suitable – wait at least 2 weeks prior to conduct the adhesion test - an average value of 0.8 N/mm² is required with no single value below 0.5 N/mm².
5.8 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Crack bridging ability: Dry Film Thickness | 310 µ; Crack Width at Break | 1.5 mm; Crack Bridging Ability | 5.0; Class A1 (-20°C) - 2 coats; Class B2 (-15°C) - 3 coats (EN 1062-7) (AS/NZS 4548.5) Appendix F
    - Tensile adhesion strength: 2.9 (2.8) N/mm² (EN 1542)
    - Capillary absorption: w = 0.02 kg/(m²h0.5) (EN 1062-3)
    - Permeability to water vapour: Dry Film Thickness | d = 210 µm; Equivalent Air Layer Thick- | SD = 1.0 m; ness; Diffusion Resistance Coeffi- | µ = 2,944; cient (AS/NZS 4548.5) Appendix C
    - Permeability to carbon dioxide: Dry film thickness | d = 210 µm; CO2 Diffusion Coefficient | D = 3.7 x 10⁻⁰⁷cm²/sec; Diffusion Resistance Coeffi- | µ = 5.4 x 10⁵; cient; Equivalent air layer thick- | R = 112 m; ness; Equivalent Thickness of | Sc = 28 cm; Concrete (AS/NZS 4548.5) Appendix D
    - Behaviour after artificial weathering: Pass after 2000 hours (EN 1062-11)
    - Freeze thaw de-icing salt resistance: 2.9 (2.1) N/mm² (EN 13687 part 1 & part 2)
5.9 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.10 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikagard®-550 W Elastic, April 2023, Version 02.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/m/sikagard_-550_w_elastic.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikagard®-550 W Elastic, version 18/02/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/k/sds-sikagard-550welastic.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikagard® 550W Elastocolor substrate, version 18/02/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/d/sds-sikagard-550welastocolorsubstrate.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Ecology, health and safety - Directive 2004/42/ce limitation of emissions of.
    - VOC
    - According to the EU-Directive 2004/42, the maximum allowed content of VOC (Product category IIA / c type wb) is 40 g/l (Limits 2010) for the ready to use product.
    - The maximum content of Sikagard®-550 W Elastic is < 40 g/l VOC for the ready to use product.
6.4 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.5 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.6 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
